newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank sees rate hike in summer 1997.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank sees rate hike in summer 1997.

text.p: Commerzbank AG chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen said on Wednesday he expected the Bundesbank to raise interest rates to combat inflation in the summer of 1997, a German magazine reported.
The Wirtschaftswoche quoted Kohlhaussen as saying he no longer expected the Bundesbank to ease its monetary policy again, as the German economy enters a firm recovery.
Kohlhaussen also said the ideal conditions capital markets enjoyed during 1996 were coming to an end.
"We are in a transition to a phase of increases," he said.
The Bundesbank has kept its main interest rates, the discount and Lombard rates, on hold at 2.50 percent and 4.50 percent respectively since April.
While these rates are not expected to be lowered again, there are some expectations for a further easing of the money market rate, or repo, now at three percent.
